newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche says 97 EPS may top 5 dmk vs 4.25.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche says 97 EPS may top 5 dmk vs 4.25.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG management board member Juergen Krumnow said on Wednesday the bank may increase its earnings per share to more than five marks ($2.96) in 1997 from 4.25 marks in 1996, depending on how markets develop and on what progress it makes in cutting costs.

Asked by Reuters Financial Television whether analysts' forecasts for an increase in earnings per share to more than five marks was realistic, Krumnow said: "I would say it's not unrealistic - it depends on market conditions in the rest of the year and on cost management."
Krumnow said Deutsche would continue to reduce its costs and keep spending under control.
"These two sides together will give us a good chance to increase results by a good percentage number."
The earnings per share figures are calculated under International Accounting Standards.

Earlier on Wednesday, Deutsche chief executive Hilmar Kopper told a news conference the bank expected an improved overall profit in 1997. In 1996, its net income per share rose to 4.25 marks from 4.15 marks.
